extracted.intended_audience: short story writers and translators seeking inclusion in the O. Henry Prize annual anthology
extracted.subtask_short: O. Henry Prize short story submission
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and selection process for stories considered for the annual O. Henry Prize Collection anthology, describing eligibility, timeline, languages, and how winners are chosen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication venue eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories published in magazines and online are eligible for inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly states that both traditional magazines and online-published stories may be considered; no additional venue restrictions are given on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and translation eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories may be written in English or translated into English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 2021 relaunch makes stories in translation eligible for the first time; translated work is explicitly permitted for consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories will be considered from September 1 to August 31 of the following year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the eligibility window for stories to be considered for a given year's awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection authority — guest editor choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Each edition has a guest editor who chooses the winners; the guest editor's vision is reflected in the selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page emphasizes that a guest editor (e.g., Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie for the relaunch) brings a 'brilliant, unique vision' that shapes the twenty winners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection pipeline — series editor nominations
rubrics_metrics.description: The guest editor chooses the twenty winners from a large pool of stories passed to her by the series editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is not from the entire universe of eligible stories directly but from a curated pool prepared by the series editor (Jenny Minton Quigley).

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of winners per edition
rubrics_metrics.description: Twenty O. Henry Prize winners are chosen for each edition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guest editor selects twenty stories to comprise the year's prize winners/anthology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of winners
rubrics_metrics.description: The winners’ stories are collected and published annually by Anchor Books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winners receive publication in the annual Anchor Books anthology (The Best Short Stories / The O. Henry Prize Collection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusive mission across career stages and geography
rubrics_metrics.description: The prize seeks to provide a prominent platform for short story writers from all around the world and at all points in their careers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award explicitly positions itself as globally inclusive and open to writers at various career stages (emerging to established).

rubrics_metrics.name: How to submit / contact for submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: For complete submission guidelines and to submit PDF files, contact jenny@ohenryprizewinners.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page directs prospective submitters to email the series editor for detailed submission procedures and PDF submission; no web form or other method is given on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual award continuity and history
rubrics_metrics.description: The O. Henry Prize is awarded annually (since 1919, with a break in 2020).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This historical note signals longstanding continuity and prestige, which can inform expectations about editorial standards and the anthology's profile.
